sources.title: Paron: Black Sea-Caspian Steppe, Natural Conditions
sources.note: Open scholarly chapter on steppe climate, water, pasture, seasonal constraints, and mobility.

sources.title: Paron: Structures and Forms of Existence
sources.note: Open scholarly chapter reconstructing political organization, camps, pastoral life, craft, belief, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Paron: The Apex of Pecheneg Political Importance
sources.note: Open scholarly chapter on Pecheneg power, diplomacy, Rus, Byzantium, and the Black Sea steppe.

sources.title: Paron: Decline of Pecheneg Power on the Black Sea Steppe
sources.note: Open scholarly chapter on Rus conflict, Oghuz pressure, Kegen, Tyrach, and movement across the Danube.

sources.title: Paron: Pechenegs in Neighbouring States
sources.note: Open scholarly chapter on settlement, service, adaptation, and continued communities in Byzantium, Hungary, and Rus.

sources.title: Paron: Conclusion
sources.note: Open scholarly conclusion stressing confederated power, mobility, interaction, and comparison without an empire model.

sources.title: The Russian Primary Chronicle, Laurentian text translation
sources.note: University-hosted translation recording Pecheneg involvement around Rus and the 1036 battle near Kyiv.

sources.title: Anna Komnene: The Alexiad, Book VIII
sources.note: Primary Byzantine narrative of the 1091 campaign and victory at Levounion.

sources.title: Anna Komnene: The Alexiad, Book VII
sources.note: Primary Byzantine narrative of the 1087 to 1090 war, wagons, families, herds, archery, and foraging.

sources.title: Michael Attaleiates: Historia, Greek and Latin edition
sources.note: Edition of an eleventh-century Byzantine narrative using a contemporary Greek outsider name for Pechenegs.

sources.title: Kovacs: Gerard of Csanad and the Pechenegs
sources.note: Russian Academy journal study of Gerard's 1030s sermon, Latin naming, mission, and Christian frontier context.

sources.title: Stephenson: Byzantine Policy towards Paristrion in the Mid-Eleventh Century
sources.note: Study combining archaeology, coins, and texts to reassess markets, administration, and conflict in Paristrion.

sources.title: Krumova: Pecheneg Chieftains in Byzantine Administration
sources.note: Study of named leaders, seals, titles, service, settlement, and identity changes inside Byzantium.

sources.title: Curta: The Image and Archaeology of the Pechenegs
sources.note: Critical study of burials, ornaments, pottery, written images, and the dangers of ethnic attribution.

sources.title: Ivanov and Ivanov: Pecheneg Pottery from Bulgaria
sources.note: Study of eleventh-century cooking and table wares associated cautiously with Pecheneg settlement in Bulgaria.

sources.title: Stoyanov: Late Nomadic Equestrian Burials in Bulgaria
sources.note: Institutional archaeological review of horse deposits, grave contexts, chronology, and attribution limits.

sources.title: Holeschak: Equestrian graves north of the lower Danube
sources.note: Peer reviewed comparison of horse remains and grave rites across broad late nomadic horizons.

sources.title: Bollok: Archaeological Traces of Pechenegs and Oghuz in Hungary
sources.note: University study of characteristic equipment, ornaments, burials, and uncertainty in identifying communities.

sources.title: Szabo: Pechenegs in the Earliest Latin Sources
sources.note: University journal study of Latin outsider terminology and accounts, including their genre and perspective.

sources.title: Bruno of Querfurt and his Pecheneg mission
sources.note: Indexed scholarly study of Bruno's mission around 1004 and the political setting of conversion efforts.

sources.title: Melnyk: Byzantium and the Pechenegs in Modern Historiography
sources.note: Open scholarly review of source bias, archaeological methods, and changing interpretations of Byzantine relations.
